title: Evening ops handoff brief - console triage
body:
Evening handoff (quick) - console / observability triage

Context:
- 18:15 - started seeing increased 95p latency on hosted-api route /v1/generate (region us-east-1).
- Spike correlated with a batch of requests from customer acct: acme-marketing (support ticket INC-9932).
- Dashboard metric groups: api->generate->latency-95, worker-pool->queue-depth.

What I observed (raw):
- Latency 95p went from ~280ms to 1.2s across the board, ~18:10-18:35.
- CPU on inference-nodes stayed ~60%, GPU util average 70%, but one node (gpu-12) had abrupt mem spike then OOM kill (see pod obs-runtime-12).
- Queue depth for continuous-batcher increased from steady 20 to ~140.
- Autoscale did not spin new pods fast enough; HPA events show scaling cooldowns.
- Customer requests show large prompt sizes (avg tokens/request 3.2k) — rerun sample from logs (req ids below).

Requests of interest (sample ids):
- req-6f4c7a (acme) 2026-03-12T18:09:12Z tokens=3280 route=/v1/generate
- req-6f4d2b (acme) 2026-03-12T18:10:02Z tokens=2970
- req-6f5e11 (other-customer) 2026-03-12T18:11:50Z tokens=145

Actions I tried (order):
1) Throttled acme-marketing at proxy level (rate-limit rule temp-acme-18) at 18:20 — immediate drop in new long requests.
2) Manually drained pod obs-runtime-12 after capturing logs; confirmed OOM transition, uploaded logs to /tmp/arthur/obs-runtime-12.log.
3) Increased HPA max replicas from 20 -> 30 to give headroom (applied via kubectl autoscale patch) at 18:25 — started seeing new pods up by 18:34.
4) Rolled back a recent dashboard agent change? NO, not yet — left as is.
5) Temporary tweak: lowered default batch window from 120ms to 80ms to reduce queueing; this reduced batching efficiency but reduced queue depth.

Immediate status now (21:00):
- Latency stabilized ~320ms 95p; queue depth ~18.
- No new OOMs since rollout of extra replicas.
- acme-marketing support ticket updated and engineering pager notified.

Open follow-ups (PRIORITY order):
- High: Investigate why one node saw a mem blowout. Possible model cache leak for long-context requests. -> assign eng/serving-runtime (Noah). (JIRA:INF-4831)
- High: Add a targeted rate-limit and quota for very long prompts per-customer (policy change). Product + Legal consult.
- Medium: Audit HPA cooldown and uplimit settings; consider predictive scaling for known batch spikes. -> eng-platform (Leah).
- Medium: Add alert for "sustained queue depth > 100 for > 5m" to reduce manual detection time.
- Low: Revisit batch window default; run perf test with long prompt distributions.

Runbook (quick commands / breadcrumbs):
- Get problematic pod logs: kubectl -n prod logs obs-runtime-12 --previous > /tmp/arthur/obs-runtime-12.log
- Check HPA events: kubectl -n prod describe hpa obs-runtime | egrep -i "Events|Conditions|Messages" -A3
- Snapshot queue depth metric: curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=queue_depth&job=batcher&from=now-1h' > /tmp/arthur/queue-snap.json
- Apply temp throttle for customer: curl -X POST https://proxy.internal/api/limits -d '{"customer":"acme-marketing","rate":5}' (ops token required)
- Reproduce a long prompt offline: python tools/replay_request.py --id req-6f4c7a --env staging

Notes for morning shift (what I want you to check):
- Verify INF-4831 assignment and ensure someone has the pod-level heap traces. I left heap dump at s3://redwood-temp/heapdumps/obs-runtime-12-20260312.hprof
- Confirm that the HPA change to max=30 is reverted back to previous if we don't want permanent increase. (I left a comment in the HPA PR.)
- Reach out to account lead for acme-marketing and confirm their use case (long prompts) — product question: are these batches intentional?
- Run a distributed load test against batcher with mixed prompt sizes; I started a test job (job id: perf-longprompts-03) in CI but it's still running.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (my notes):
- Is there a caching path that retains per-request KV state across requests? (suspect on older runtime image).
- Why did autoscaler cooldown prevent new pods? check controller logs for scale down suppression rule.
- Should we implement per-request token limit enforcement at the proxy?

Important links & artifacts:
- JIRA INC-9932 (customer support) -> https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-9932
- JIRA INF-4831 (investigate OOM) -> https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4831
- Heap dump -> s3://redwood-temp/heapdumps/obs-runtime-12-20260312.hprof
- Temporary logs -> /tmp/arthur/obs-runtime-12.log

Short handoff message to leave in #oncall: 
"Evening: observed trimmed latency spike tied to long prompts from acme-marketing. Throttled customer, scaled HPA up, removed bad pod. Queue depth back to normal. Follow ups: INF-4831 (OOM root cause), consider rate-limit quota for long prompts. Leaving notes in my handoff doc (users/arthur). Ping me if anything reappears."

Random quick notes (scratch):
- possible pattern: large prompt + concurrent small prompts -> batcher stalls -> queue grows -> mem pressure on older runtime images w/o aggressive GC.
- TODO: add quick reproduction script to tools/ -- will attach tomorrow.

-- Arthur
